## Chinese 
原文 - 1982  R. Incognito
— And one should imagine that he is happy.
The Myth of Sisyphus — Albert Camus —
# 神話與人 (Myth and Man)
人是一種很奇怪的動物，也是一種很可憐的動物，他時常要反問自己的生活目標，要解釋自己的行為，將毫無意義的自然現象賦予意義，將漫無目的之世事理性化。人是自己的創造者，生與死，愛和恨，善與惡都深深地隱藏在人類的心坎裏，人既是美麗善良的天使，也是醜陋惡毒的魔鬼。現實世界的無常，人生旅程的苦難，時間歷史的奧秘，無不使人顛僕，使他感受到人性的薄弱和束縛。當人類進入了歷史的巨輪，意識到自己的存在時，他更體驗到生命的短暫及限制，脫離不了殘酷的現實生活，也不能衝破死亡的枷鎖，他被規範在這時空欄中。或許人類要找尋幻滅了的黃金時代，夢想回到已失落的伊甸園中，他不自覺地創造了一套超自然的宇宙觀，一套超越時空的神話。
這些神話將現實生活抽離，昇華到一個意像的境界，成為人類思想活動的雛型，在人和自然的割離和結合中。神話也變成一套有系統的解釋體系。逐漸地成長及制度化，有些神話更發展成著名的宗教思想，神話的形式是超越歷史及時空的，人類的神話非常普遍，而且是圍繞幾個重要的模式發展，但神話的內容同時也是某一時空及環境下的社會產品。各地的神話都具備有頗完整的世界觀，闡明宇宙及人類的來源，經歷及滅亡，而且還引導出一套生活方式和社會制度。
神話是連接永遠與時間的橋樑，把人類無意識的存在帶到歷史的創造及發予。創世神話解釋宇宙和人類的起源。差不多所有文化的神話都認為在宇宙還沒有成形之前，天地乃是一片太虛混沌。有一種超自然的力量導入秩序和發展，並且創造了生命及人類。聖經中的神在七天的時間內創造了光明，大地、動植物和人類。希臘神話中的「力量」從卡奧斯中帶出秩序，還創造了綴滿星辰的天空和充滿生機的大地及海洋。 
人的生死，兩性關係等都是很神秘的想像。這些現像和萬物的生長與滅亡，都連結在神話裏構成一個不可分割的體系，性高潮中的一剎那，渾然忘我的極樂，歇死歇仙的感覺，都很自然地聯想到生育、動植物生長，天地及人類起源的奧秘中，人類常被想像為大地的兒子，是從大地母親的子宮中孕育出來。而那種性極樂的感覺，往往是所謂「宗教極樂」的基礎，在神秘主義或宗教中的「與神結合為一體」，也是這種原始極樂的昇華。
神話中的男女關係，絕大部份都是亂倫的，希臘神話中的宙斯及他的皇后希拉是一對兄妹。聖經中的夏娃，也可能和她的兒子發生關係，相信最著名的亂倫關係，就是伊庇帕斯的故事，伊庇帕斯不自覺地殺了自己的父親，並娶了自己的母親，應驗了預言，結果他用針刺瞎了雙眼，到處流浪。又聖經中大衛的兒子暗嫩詐病玷辱了他的妹妹他瑪，結果被押沙龍擊殺。從此可見早期人類的亂倫關係很普遍，而且還被容忍，神與神之間也被投射為有此關係，但隨着家庭的興起，亂倫會直接影響到家庭成員間的地位及權力，使家庭制度崩潰。所以後期的亂倫被視為禁忌，若果犯了，就有極嚴重的悲劇產生。
生是一種束縛，從無我變成自我，死是一種解脫，從自我回復到無我。大部份的文化都對死有一定的觀念，許多宗教都認為死是短暫的，甚至是虛幻的，因為要理性化世界的不平等及矛盾，生命也被視為一個幻像，或是將來「黃金時代」來臨的前奏，為了確保多災多難的人們（尤其是被壓迫的一羣）有一些保償，地府及天堂的觀念也油然而生，中國的十八層地獄就是由閻羅王掌管，設有各種的刑具來處罰作惡的人。希臘神話中的地府由哈德斯統治，設有各種的難關，在此未達邊界，其中以「坦達羅斯的刑罰」及「薛西弗斯之岩石」最著名。基督教中而稍覺是不接受救主的死到那硫磺之火熱燒的地方。總之，在地府不受歡迎的人或靈魂，大都受長久不熄烈火煎熬。相對來說，天堂或極樂世界是善長或得救的人所集居的地方，他們可以永遠過着幸福的日子，希臘的希特瓦看怕善的死靈就是在這樣的地方。
### 英雄與神話 (Hero and Myth)
人類有了時間及我的意識後，生命旅程中的各種現象和生死病死，兩性關係，社會政治情況等，都被昇華到一些生活性的神話中，這些神話多是透過英雄的「冒險傳奇」出現，反映出人類的心理狀態，神話中的主角是人類內心矛盾的投射，凝聚在一些英雄或英雄的身體上，他們有着人類的特點及弱點，也具備人類理想化的性質，天神們也時常幫助或懲罰這些英雄人物，卻不容許他們跑出命運及人性弱點的框框。聖經中的衛或珊門等都是這樣的人物，他們得到耶和華的幫助，戰勝了敵人。但大衛卻因為貪求烏利亞的妻子拔示巴，以至被耶和華懲罰，使他和拔示巴的兒子活活疾致死，還使大衛的兒子押沙龍反叛他，最後被人刺死。所羅門也因為寵愛異族的女子，使耶和華樹立哈達及利遜作敵人，並且分裂了以色列國。希臘的特色斯王子，在拉比林多司（迷宮）中捕殺了食人肉的怪獸米諾陶桑斯，但回程時忘記放下黑色的帆，而使他的父親愛格斯王以為他已死亡。憤然跳進愛琴海自盡而特色斯本身也被琉科梅多斯謀殺。
神話中的英雄角色，大多是王子，但出生時被拋棄，由一些低下階層的人或隱士養育，長大後有着一段豐功偉跡，最後結果是戰敗或因其它因素飄泊流戛至死，這些英雄代表了人類對超越現實枷鎖的掙扎，也催促了「救世主」哲學的形成，一個製造神話的基礎是主角的「神秘化」及「人化」，主角具備了神及人的品質。換句話說，主角是人——神，是神的化身，有着雙重身份，像聖經中的耶穌，或印度教中的昆涇紐（保存之神）。這些人——神影響着人類歷史的進程，也是神參予歷史的表現，他們以「英雄」或「救世主」身份來到世界，拯救在苦難中的人類，脫離壓迫及罪惡。基督教中的耶穌，被釘到十字架上，流出寶血為世人在藚罪惡，叫一切信他的不至滅亡，反得永生。印度教的昆涇紐，化身為拉瑪王子，戰勝了邪惡的敵人。消除人類的災難。這些人神。無論在品質或行為上都被認為是完美無缺的，在現代宗教思想上，這些人——神的地位是極重要的，因為他們是維繫人與神的媒介，也是神進入歷史的脉脈。
### 人的存在，不是單靠食物，更要靠神話。 
何謂自我體性而言，自我省察與界向都在，這便是一生行程的模式，這實踐的符號，精神自從世界出世後，這意像與平衡，重新架構起對這宇宙獨立的生命，本能的自省在人活在體內具有創造性的一面，在完美的對象世界及人類的自體，這表現便是一件普遍而不衰生活下痕跡，是基督的受難、佛陀出走其精神的昇華和造物神秘性的存在融化的一部份，生命的本質稟賦的力量上確實廣海。張延二十年，期籍算穿
他們自智（高高在上神聖生活）談到今天的人的案子虛無縹、是平面又貧乏而「行效觀表面」？
研究神話這深層神在內自我認知的旨意及洞之中，神話給我們反映出，人類認清自己是在生命展轉迷之中，我們的焦慮正是那一些沒有定義的神話象徵。在我們尋求神話也有內自了某許我們精神的成熟路
走向非神秘的人性面我們發掘出的寂凝，重新與那 我們無求索社會性與神話引伸到個人的幽谷。
要是從新有編制。我們在困惑出來，在社會的 枷原體之中，我們的心底也像昔日一般，期盼擁有那 些敲擊出我、各姓我們的一切，這般人類對生存的愛 ，我們只是無可奈何地活著。
巫師及祭禮的存在，是較原始宗教的特色，祭禮是一些行動的儀式，是實踐的符號，而神話是思想的產物，是意識的符號，整個祭禮過程通常是神話的重演，英雄的靈魂進入巫師體內重新經歷話的一切，以求達到拯救世界及人類的目標。這個現象在一些普遍的宗教也留下痕跡，基督教的聖餐，意義也是將耶穌的身體和血被轉化為信徒身體中的一部份，使他們有着無盡的力量去戰勝魔鬼，背起十字架，跟隨基督。 
### 現實 = 神話
神話在人類的自覺、現實和想像間徘徊，今天的神話是當代的現實，而今天的現實，豈不會是明天的神話？意像是神話的泉源，人性的衝突，善與惡的分辨，死亡的恐懼，生存的荒謬，都是神話的原動力，這些力量深遠地影響到古今社會的運作，不知不覺間制爪着思潮，使一串有連繫的神話內在化，而且製造更多神話。我們何嘗沒有神話呢？或者我們會相信星座運程，某某主義，掌相，基督或黃金。我們或許會對明星、富豪、教主等的私生活或發跡史特別有興趣，他們就好像帶着一些神秘色彩，難道這等人不是現代的「英雄」甚至「人——神」嗎？神話的形式沒有甚麼大改變，只是內容隨着社會現實環境變遷，主題也漸由從前的神為中心轉化成人為中心，神話可算是人類本質歪曲的縮影，人類心態的演化也濃縮在神話的發展中。 
西方文化由文藝復興及工業革命釋放出來，傳統的天主教神話也被逐個擊破，隨着基督教的興起，資本主義、國家主義及馬克思主義的流行及衝激，西方思想也套上了一層現代的神話，它們有着一套單向及完整的宇宙觀，相信一個出世或入世的天國或黃金時代，他們的救世主或英雄，影響着歷史的發展及方向，在他們的動陶下，很多事物或傳奇（甚至是日常生活）都被轉化到神話的層次。東方的思想，同樣也被佛教及印度教的思想疊罩着，在近代才逐漸被西方文化侵蝕。另一方面，因為傳統神話的破裂，使人類在極不安全的狀態中生活，他們也要製造神話，幫助他們面對（或逃避）現實生活，試問今天的電子遊戲機，是不是大量生產「打怪獸英雄？
研究神話就是將神話內的訊息帶到現實生活之中，神話給我們的啟示，正要反問自己是否生活在神話之中，我們的現實又是否一串很有系統的神話故事，而我們是否神話中的角色？或許我們是神話的奴隸, 或許發明神話的人也是他們發明品的奴隸，重要的是我們能否將社會性的神話引申到個人的神話。
算這是宿命論吧，我們從黑暗而來，也終會回到黑暗之中，我們的心靈也像迷宮一般，隨時隨地都有怪獸出現，吞噬我們的一切，這是人類的必然命運，我們只是無可奈何地活着。
**"Man the myth-creator
Man the myth-preserver
Man the myth-destroyer"**
*R. Incognito*
## English
translated by Gemini 2026
### Epigraph
— And one should imagine that he is happy.
The Myth of Sisyphus — Albert Camus —
### Theme: Myth and Man
#### Section 1: The Human Fetters of Existence and Cosmic Order
Man is a very peculiar animal, and a very pitiable one at that. He constantly questions the purpose of his life, demands explanations for his actions, attributes meaning to meaningless natural phenomena, and rationalizes a directionless world. Man is his own creator; life and death, love and hate, good and evil are all deeply embedded within the human psyche. Man is simultaneously a beautiful, benevolent angel and an ugly, malicious demon. The impermanence of the physical world, the suffering of life's journey, and the mysteries of time and history constantly cause him to stumble, making him acutely aware of the frailty and limitations of human nature. As humanity entered the massive gears of history and became conscious of its own existence, it grew even more aware of life's brevity and constraints. Unable to escape the cruel realities of daily existence or break free from the shackles of mortality, man finds himself confined within the boundaries of space and time. Perhaps in a bid to seek a vanished golden age, dreaming of a return to a lost Eden, he unconsciously constructed a supernatural worldview—a system of myths that transcends time and space.
These myths detach daily life from reality, sublimating it into an imagistic realm that serves as the prototype for human intellectual activity. Amidst the alienation from and reunification with nature, myth transforms into a systematic explanatory framework. Gradually evolving and institutionalizing, certain myths eventually developed into prominent religious philosophies. The form of myth is transcendent of history, time, and space; human mythologies are universally widespread and tend to develop around several core archetypes. Yet, the actual content of a myth remains a social product tied to a specific time, place, and environment. Mythologies across various regions possess highly comprehensive worldviews, clarifying the origins, experiences, and ultimate demise of both the universe and humanity, while simultaneously prescribing lifestyles and social institutions.
Myth is the bridge that connects eternity with time, bringing humanity's unconscious existence into the creation and endowment of history. Creation myths explain the origin of the cosmos and humankind. Virtually all cultural mythologies posit that before the universe took shape, heaven and earth existed in a state of absolute, primordial chaos. A supernatural power then introduced order and progression, creating life and humanity. The God of the Bible created light, the earth, flora, fauna, and humankind within a span of seven days. In Greek mythology, "Forces" brought order out of Chaos, creating a sky studded with constellations, alongside a vibrant earth and ocean.
#### Section 2: Life, Sexuality, and Mortality within Mythological Systems
Human life and death, alongside gender relations, are subjects of deeply mysterious imagination. These phenomena, paired with the growth and decay of all living things, are linked within mythology to constitute an inseparable system. The fleeting moment of sexual climax—a blissful state of total self-oblivion, a sensation suspended between death and transcendence—naturally evokes associations with fertility, the growth of flora and fauna, and the mysteries surrounding the cosmic origin of humankind. Humans are often imagined as children of the earth, gestated within the womb of Mother Earth. That sensation of sexual ecstasy frequently serves as the foundation for so-called "religious ecstasy." The mystical or religious concept of "becoming one with the divine" is merely a sublimation of this primitive, primal ecstasy.
The relations between sexes in mythology are overwhelmingly incestuous. In Greek mythology, Zeus and his queen, Hera, are brother and sister. Eve in the Bible might also have had relations with her son. Believably, the most famous incestuous relationship is the story of Oedipus, who unwittingly killed his father and married his mother, fulfilling the prophecy; ultimately, he blinded himself with pins and spent his life wandering. Furthermore, in the Bible, David's son Amnon feigned illness to violate his sister Tamar, resulting in his assassination by Absalom. This demonstrates that incestuous relationships were widespread among early humans and were largely tolerated; relationships among deities were projected in a similar vein. However, with the rise of the nuclear family, incest began to directly disrupt status and power dynamics among family members, threatening the collapse of the family institution. Consequently, in later eras, incest was treated as a taboo—and if violated, it resulted in severe tragedies.
Life is a form of bondage, shifting from selflessness to the ego; death is a liberation, returning from the ego to selflessness. Most cultures maintain specific concepts regarding death. Many religions view death as transient or even illusory. To rationalize the inequalities and contradictions of the world, mortal life is treated as a mirage, or merely a prelude to a future "Golden Age." To ensure that disaster-ridden populations (particularly the oppressed) receive some compensation, concepts of hell and heaven naturally emerge. The eighteen levels of Chinese hell are governed by King Yama, equipped with various instruments of torture to punish evildoers. The underworld of Greek mythology is ruled by Hades, featuring various obstacles at its boundaries, among which the "Tantalus punishment" and the "Rock of Sisyphus" are the most renowned. In Christianity, hell is a place where those who reject the Savior are cast into a burning lake of fire and sulfur. In short, souls unwelcome in the underworld generally suffer an everlasting doom. Conversely, heaven or the blissful realm is where the virtuous or the saved congregate, allowing them to enjoy eternal happiness; the Elysium of Greece and the Kingdom of Heaven in Hebrew tradition are prime examples of this.
#### Section 3: The Human-Divine Boundary and Tragic Destiny
Once humanity gained an awareness of time and self, the various obstacles, birth, aging, illness, and death encountered along life's journey—alongside gender dynamics and socio-political conditions—were sublimated into localized, secular myths. These myths predominantly manifested through the "adventure legends" of heroes, reflecting the psychological state of mankind. The protagonists of myth are projections of internal human contradictions, concentrated within the bodies of certain heroes. They possess human traits and frailties, yet also embody idealized human virtues. The gods frequently aid or punish these heroic figures, yet they never permit them to break free from the structural confines of destiny and human weakness. Figures like David or Samson in the Bible are classic examples; they received Jehovah’s aid to vanquish enemies. Yet David, driven by his lust for Uriah’s wife, Bathsheba, incurred Jehovah's punishment: the child born of their union was struck with fatal illness, and David's own son, Absalom, rebelled against him, eventually meeting a pierced death. Solomon, due to his infatuation with foreign women, prompted Jehovah to raise adversaries like Hadad and Rezon against him, ultimately fracturing the Kingdom of Israel. The Greek prince Theseus slaughtered the man-eating beast Minotaur inside the Labyrinth; however, on his return voyage, he forgot to lower the black sails, causing his father, King Aegeus, to believe he was dead. In grief, the king threw himself into the Aegean Sea, and Theseus himself was eventually murdered by Lycomedes.
The heroic figures in myths are mostly princes who were abandoned at birth and raised by lower-class peasants or hermits. Upon reaching adulthood, they achieve a series of monumental exploits, only to ultimately face defeat or die wandering in exile due to external circumstances. These heroes represent humanity's spiritual struggle against the shackles of reality, which accelerated the formulation of "Messianic" philosophy. A core foundation of myth-making is the dual process of "mystification" and "humanization" of the protagonist, wherein the hero embodies both divine and human qualities. In other words, the protagonist is a Man-God—an incarnation of the divine possessing a dual identity, akin to Jesus in the Bible or Vishnu (the Preserver) in Hinduism. These Men-Gods alter the trajectory of human history, representing divine intervention in historical affairs. They arrive in the world as "heroes" or "saviors" to rescue suffering humanity from oppression and darkness. Jesus in Christianity was crucified, shedding precious blood to cleanse humanity of sin, so that whosoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life. In Hinduism, Vishnu incarnated as Prince Rama to vanquish evil adversaries and eliminate human catastrophe. These Men-Gods are deemed flawless in both character and deed. In modern religious thought, the position of these Men-Gods is paramount because they act as the medium tethering man to the divine, serving as the pulsing vein through which God enters history.
#### Section 4: The Primordial Re-enactment
The existence of shamans and sacrificial rituals is a hallmark of primitive religion. Rituals are active ceremonies—symbols of praxis—whereas myths are products of thought—symbols of consciousness. The entire sacrificial process is typically a re-enactment of myth; the soul of the hero enters the shaman's body to re-experience everything within the narrative, aiming to achieve the salvation of the world and mankind. This phenomenon has left distinct traces even in mainstream religions: the Christian Eucharist essentially transforms the body and blood of Jesus into a part of the believer's own body, granting them endless strength to conquer demons, shoulder their cross, and follow Christ.
#### Section 5: The Internalization of Modern Mythologies
Myth fluctuates between human consciousness, reality, and imagination. The myth of today is the reality of the present, and will not the reality of today become the myth of tomorrow? Imagery is the wellspring of myth; human conflict, the distinction between good and evil, the dread of mortality, and the absurdity of existence serve as its driving forces. These forces deeply impact the operation of ancient and modern societies alike, unconsciously shackling trends of thought, internalizing a chain of interconnected myths, and continuously manufacturing new ones.
How can we claim to be devoid of myths? We choose to believe in horoscopes, certain political ideologies, palmistry, Christ, or gold. We might display an intense fascination with the private lives or rags-to-riches stories of celebrities, tycoons, and cult leaders. They seem wrapped in a mysterious aura—are these individuals not the "heroes" or even "Men-Gods" of the modern era? The underlying structure of myth has undergone little structural change; only its content shifts alongside modern socio-environmental realities. The core theme has gradually tilted from a theo-centric model toward an anthropo-centric one. Myth can be viewed as a distorted miniature of fundamental human nature, and the evolution of the human psyche is condensed within its historical development.
#### Section 6: The Modern Existential Vacuum
Western culture was liberated by the Renaissance and the Industrial Revolution, which systematically dismantled traditional Catholic myths. With the rise of Protestantism, alongside the spread and friction of capitalism, nationalism, and Marxism, Western thought donned a layer of modern mythology. These modern ideologies possess unidirectional, totalizing worldviews, promising an otherworldly or earthly kingdom—a secular Golden Age. Their saviors or heroes dictate the progression and direction of history; under their agitation, many mundane matters or legends (even daily routines) are elevated to a mythological tier. Eastern thought, similarly enveloped by Buddhist and Hindu philosophies, was only gradually eroded by Western culture in the modern era.
On the other hand, the shattering of traditional myths has forced humanity to live in a state of profound psychological insecurity. Consequently, humans must manufacture new myths to help those stranded in bewilderment and alienation find an existential anchor for their being. Modern society frequently re-engineers myth, extending collective social myths down into the desolate valleys of the individual ego, hoping to forge a path out of perplexity. Within the shackles of societal structures, the human heart still yearns—just as it did in antiquity—for anything that can strike a chord and inspire life. It is precisely this raw love for existence that prevents us from living in absolute, helpless resignation.

### Perplexity | 2026年8月 | Wissen

Myth supplies cosmic order, moral compensation, and historical direction; this broad hypothesis pre-classifies religion, ideology, celebrity, and gaming under one explanatory type.

#### 詮釋學分析：
- 視域融合（Horizonverschmelzung）層面：作者以1982年香港大學生之視域，融合希臘神話、聖經敘事、印度教與中國冥府觀等多重異質視域，其詮釋策略非逐一比較宗教學的客觀並陳，而是主動將自身時代焦慮（脫離現實、命運框限）投射回古典文本，構成一種前理解（Vorverständnis）主導的挪用式閱讀。
- 敘事主體「R. Incognito」之修辭位置具雙重性：前半段以「研究者」姿態進行第三人稱論述（「人是……」），後半段轉為「我們」之集體第一人稱（「我們的心靈也像迷宮一般」），此一人稱轉換為典型呂格爾式「敘事認同」建構過程——作者透過述說神話之歷史，同時建構自身之詮釋主體性。

- 詮釋循環於文本結構本身重演：文章起於界定「神話」，終於質問「我們是否神話的奴隸」，形成部分（定義）與整體（自我處境）之循環回扣。
## English
### Perplexity | August 2026 | Interpret
- “R. Incognito” begins in an encyclopedic, quasi-omniscient register that establishes cross-cultural authority, shifts into fractured lyrical self-address, then invokes “we” to share the labyrinth, monster, and fate. The persona therefore moves from expositor to a witness trapped alongside the reader.
- The essay seeks a fusion of mythic traditions and modern life: biblical, Greek, and Hindu narratives are translated into horoscopes, ideologies, celebrities, tycoons, and video games. This is not mere analogy; it rewrites everyday desire as continuing participation in myth, through historically situated linguistic horizons.
- Its interpersonal rhetoric does not fully open a dialogue: repeated questions install the reader inside a preformed “we,” while “perhaps” and “is it not” preserve limited distance. In Ricoeurian terms, hero, savior, and Sisyphus operate as plots of collective identity, but the conclusion withholds heroic agency from the reader.
### Claude Sonnet 5 | Aug 2026 | Interpret
#### Hermeneutic Analysis:
- Fusion of horizons: writing from a 1982 Hong Kong university-student horizon, the author merges Greek myth, Biblical narrative, Hindu cosmology, and Chinese underworld conceptions — not as neutral comparative religion, but as an appropriative reading that projects the author's own contemporary anxieties (alienation, fate's constraints) back onto classical texts, a fore-understanding-driven (Vorverständnis) interpretive move.
- The narrating persona "R. Incognito" shifts rhetorical position mid-text: the first half speaks in detached third-person ("man is..."), while the latter half shifts to collective first-person ("our minds too are like a labyrinth") — a textbook Ricoeurian narrative-identity construction, where telling myth's history simultaneously constructs the author's own interpretive subjectivity.
- Intertextual strategy: sources are never cited directly; the text closes instead on an aphoristic assertion ("call this fatalism, if you will") — persuasive rather than academic rhetoric, consistent with the polemical style of 1980s HK student-publication debate culture, implicitly interpellating the reader as a co-fated "we" rather than a "you" to be argued with.
- The hermeneutic circle recurs structurally: the essay opens by defining "myth" and closes by questioning "are we slaves to myth" — part (definition) and whole (self-situation) folding back into one another.

### Perplexity | 2026年8月 | Deconstruct

### Claude Sonnet 5 | 2026年8月 | Deconstruct
#### 解構分析：
- 核心二元對立「神話／現實」自我崩解：文本標題本身「現實＝神話」已將對立項等同化，形成德希達式之延異（différance）——神話既非現實之對立面亦非其單純反映，而是不斷延宕、互為蹤跡（trace）之關係，二元結構之穩定性從標題起即被文本自身瓦解。
- 補充邏輯（supplément）之運作：神話被界定為對「無意義自然現象」之補充性賦義，但此補充逐漸取代並構成「現實」本身（「今天的神話是當代的現實」），補充物反噬並取代其所欲補充之原初，符合德希達補充邏輯之經典結構。
- 平滑與條紋空間（Deleuze）：文本中段之語法崩解（文法斷裂、句構失序）恰形成一「平滑空間」的爆發性入侵，中斷前段條紋化（結構化、分類式）之神話論述秩序，此斷裂處未被文本自身承認或縫合，構成一顯著的結構性裂隙（aporia）。
- 缺席之蹤跡：文本大量處理「亂倫」、「弒父」、「昏迷般極樂」等主題，卻始終未將自身「研究神話者」之位置解構——作者宣稱要研究神話卻未反身質疑「研究」本身是否已是另一則神話裝置，此為文本最大之未言明缺口。

### Perplexity | August 2026 | Deconstruct
- The essay is organized through order/chaos, myth/reality, god/human, redemption/bondage, and good/evil, yet its subordinated terms repeatedly invade the privileged ones. Myth is meant to order chaos but generates fresh anxiety, institutions, and enslavement; “reality” therefore never stands outside myth as a pure ground. Deconstruction follows such internal gaps and undecidables.

#### Post-Structural Analysis:
- The core binary "myth/reality" collapses on its own terms: the section title "Reality = Myth" equates the two poles directly, producing a Derridean différance — myth is neither reality's opposite nor its simple reflection, but a relation of endless deferral and mutual trace; the binary's stability is undone by the text's own structure from the title onward.

- A trace of absence: despite extensive treatment of incest, patricide, and ecstatic self-loss, the text never deconstructs its own position as "researcher of myth" — the author claims to study myth without reflexively questioning whether "研究" (research/study) itself is already another mythic apparatus. #### 中文評論：存在主義與神話結構的時代互文
本篇論文寫於 1982 年，是一篇極具時代烙印的思想習作，深刻反映了 20 世紀 80 年代初期香港知識青年在面對西方現代性衝擊時的批判性思考。文章將卡謬（Albert Camus）的存在主義哲學與比較神話學（如列維-斯特勞斯或坎貝爾的結構主義視角）進行了跨學科的互文編織，展現出高度的思辨野心。
#### 優點與思想亮點：
1. 結構的現代化重組：將原本作為「視覺平衡」的橫欄創世導言移至第一欄末尾，在文本邏輯上完成了一次從微觀（人類生存困境）到巨觀（宇宙秩序建立）的流暢過渡。這證明文章本身的內在張力極強，各部分的互嵌性高。
2. 敏銳的現代性批判：文章最精彩的洞察在於其對「現代神話」的去政治化與去神聖化解構。作者敏銳地指出，雖然古典宗教式微，但人類並未擺脫神話；相反，現代人將政治主義（資本主義、馬克思主義）、大眾文化（明星、富豪、電子遊戲）轉化為新的「人——神」崇拜。這種將「電子遊戲打怪獸」與「原始巫術/聖餐禮」並置的對比，準確預言了當代消費社會的「拜物教」本質。
3. 深沉的存在主義關懷：全篇以薛西弗斯（Sisyphus）的隱喻為核心，雖然充滿了「無可奈何地活著」、「黑暗」等悲觀語彙，但最終落腳於對生命本能的愛，呈現出一種「明知荒謬而反抗」的悲劇英雄主義。
#### 局限與時代局限性：
1. 概念邊界的模糊化：文章在論述「神話」、「宗教」與「政治意識形態（如馬克思主義、國家主義）」時，傾向於將它們混為一談。從現代社會學角度看，意識形態的理性官僚體制與原始神話的非理性意像具有本質區別，全盤「神話化」雖然深刻，但略顯泛化。
2. 性別與歷史視角的單一：在探討「兩性關係與亂倫」時，作者主要依賴古典文本的字面解讀，缺乏對家庭制度演變背後經濟與社會權力結構的深度剖析，帶有那個時代通俗人類學的拼貼痕跡。
總結： 這是一篇兼具理性批判與詩意憂鬱的優秀文獻。它不僅僅是在記錄神話，其本身就是那一 health/思潮世代的青年，在現代都市的「枷鎖與迷宮」中，為尋求自我主體性而敲擊出的一聲思想回響。

#### English Commentary: Existentialism and the Structuralization of Modern Myth
Written in 1982, this essay stands as a sophisticated intellectual artifact of its era, capturing the critical anxiety of Hong Kong’s young intelligentsia as they grappled with the onset of Western late-modernity. By weaving Albert Camus’s existentialism together with structural and comparative mythology (reminiscent of Claude Lévi-Strauss and Joseph Campbell), the author displays a remarkable degree of conceptual ambition.
Strengths and Intellectual Merits:
1. Logical Rigor post-Reorganization: Moving the creation preamble to the base of Section 1 successfully repairs a fragmented layout, turning it into an elegant thematic bridge. The text scales beautifully from micro-existential dread (the human condition) to macro-cosmic architecture (the establishment of divine order), proving that the piece possesses strong internal cohesion.
2. Astute Critique of Secularity: The piece shines brightest in its deconstruction of "modern myths." The author correctly diagnoses that the retreat of traditional theology did not eliminate myth-making; instead, modern society redirected its religious impulses toward political ideologies (Capitalism, Marxism) and pop-culture icons (celebrities, tycoons, video game avatars). Paralleling "shamanic possession" and the "Christian Eucharist" with the tech-industrial production of "monster-slaying video games" is a brilliant premonition of late-capitalist commodity fetishism.
3. Grounded Existential Resolution: Anchored by The Myth of Sisyphus, the narrative initially cloaks itself in the pessimistic vocabulary of the era ("helplessness," "existential abyss," "darkness"). However, it avoids total nihilism by concluding that the sheer, raw love for existence acts as an act of resistance—a classic Camusian stance of embracing the absurd.
Limitations and Methodological Blind Spots:
1. Conceptual Over-extension: The author routinely collapses the boundary between "myth," "institutionalized religion," and "secular socio-political ideology." While framing nationalism or capitalism as modern myths is rhetorically powerful, sociology distinguishes the highly rationalized, bureaucratic framework of modern ideology from the irrational, symbolic imagery of primitive myth.
2. Uncritical Anthropological Inferences: The exploration of sexuality and incest taboos relies somewhat heavily on literal, mythic text readings (e.g., King David, Oedipus). It glosses over the underlying socio-economic and material shifts that dictated family power structures, reflecting the loose, cut-and-paste nature of popular anthropology common in student publications of the early 1980s.
Conclusion: Ultimately, the piece is a compelling fusion of rigorous structural analysis and poetic melancholy. It does not merely archive ancient lore; rather, the essay itself functions as an intellectual artifact of a generation of young scholars trying to strike a spark and locate their own subjectivities within the "shackles and labyrines" of a rapidly changing metropolis.
